newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end steady in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end steady in thin trade.

text.p: Rubber futures closed steady on Monday in thin, lacklustre trade for all rubber grades with the sole exception of RSS3 rubber, dealers said.
"We did a bit of April RSS3 grade rubber for some local buyers, but the volumes involved were not that spectacular," a trader for a foreign brokerage house said.
"There was some buying done, but the tonnages were fairly small and it was still a very quiet market on the whole," another rubber dealer said.
Traders said the the only thing that lifted the market was the shortcovering seen for RSS3 grade rubber.

Total volume traded for RSS3 rubber reached about 8,500 tonnes with volume for the most active May futures contract exceeding 3,600 tonnes. Volume for the October/December contract reached around 3,000 tonnes.
At around 0945 GMT, May RSS3 was seen at 123.00-125.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 123.25 cents.
May RSS1 was indicated unchanged at 175.75 Singapore cents (US$1.23) a kg. October/December RSS1 was seen steady at 180.00 Singapore cents (US$1.26) a kg.
May TSR20 was indicated also unchanged at 166.50 Singapore cents (US$1.16) a kg. - (US$1-S$1.43) - Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
